Summary
KIP-1150 introduced diskless topics. KIP-1163 defines their produce, fetch, and replica behavior, and KIP-1164 defines the Diskless coordinator. Those KIPs use mixed-partition write-ahead log (WAL) objects as the durable ingest format and leave the transfer to KIP-405 Tiered Storage to a follow-up KIP.
This KIP defines that transfer. Every diskless topic is a consolidated diskless topic (CDT) from creation. Producers write through the diskless WAL. Each assigned replica materializes the untiered suffix as ordinary per-partition Kafka log segments. The partition leader copies closed segments through the existing KIP-405 Remote Storage Manager (RSM) and Remote Log Metadata Manager (RLMM) interfaces. After the remote copy becomes durable and discoverable, the Diskless coordinator removes the matching WAL batch coordinates. KIP-405 then provides long-term storage, reads, and physical retention for the consolidated prefix.
This KIP also defines the offset frontiers, failure ordering, replica recovery, retention, and coordinator records needed to prune WAL data without losing or hiding records.
This KIP changes two earlier sketches:
KIP-1163 currently points its WAL-object merging section at KIP-1165. This KIP supersedes that reference. WAL-object merging is not part of KIP-1165.
KIP-1150 lists KIP-1163 and KIP-1164 as the minimum implementation. Because every upstream diskless topic consolidates from creation, KIP-1165 joins that minimum dependency set.
Motivation
The WAL is an ingest format
A WAL object combines batches from many topic partitions. This lets one object-storage upload cover many Produce requests and keeps the number of uploads independent of the partition count. The format is efficient for ingest, but it is a poor long-term per-partition log:
A lagging consumer needs coordinator lookups and ranged object reads to reconstruct one partition.
The Diskless coordinator retains one coordinate for every live WAL batch.
A reassigned replica must rebuild from mixed-partition objects.
Physical deletion of one partition's expired data waits for every other live batch in the shared object.
Kafka already has a long-term format
KIP-405 stores ordinary Kafka log segments. Existing RSM and RLMM plugins, remote reads, leader-epoch indexes, transaction indexes, producer snapshots, local retention, and operational tools already use that format.
Materializing WAL batches into Kafka segments lets diskless ingest reuse this storage system without teaching KIP-405 plugins about mixed-partition WAL objects.
Proposed changes
Consolidated Diskless Topic
The consolidated diskless topic (CDT) is a topic that has a tiered prefix in the classic Kafka per partition log format, and a WAL tail. The typical, intuitive form of this consolidated log can be found below. On this figure, we can see a topic where consolidation is in progress. The log has a tiered prefix and a diskless tail that overlaps the tiered space. We also have a local log that is used by the log tiering system and for serving reads within that offset interval.
Consolidation Fetcher
The intuition for implementing this is to use something similar to the replica fetchers, except it fetches from the object storage, starting from the earliest WAL objects. This is called the Consolidation Fetcher. It extends the abstract classes in Kafka. It has the following main components:
